trace.title: Business unit test
trace.detail:
# The idea

A unit test checks a small piece of behavior using ordinary objects and controlled dependencies. It should be quick.

A web test checks HTTP binding, validation, status, and JSON. An integration test checks actual wiring or external boundaries.

Do not load the entire application for every arithmetic or ownership rule. Do not use only mocks to claim that SQL, transactions, and bean discovery work.

Use a small number of database tests against the database type you rely on for concurrency and constraints.

Test observable behavior.

A good failure test names what must not happen: a denied request must not write, a failed transaction must not leave half a change, and a duplicate command must not charge twice.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
First make the test fail for the right reason. Then change the implementation.

For a bug in JSON validation, a service mock alone cannot see the problem; exercise MVC. For a missing unique index, an in-memory repository fake cannot see it; test the database.

Avoid asserting exact private method order when the contract allows alternatives. Control time and remote responses.

Race tests need controlled overlap; random sleeps create flaky evidence.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A test marked @Transactional may roll back its own work and hide production commit/after-commit behavior. Verify relevant effects after the actual use-case transaction has completed.
